title: Enigma's one flaw: a letter never became itself
description:
Enigma's reflector meant a letter could never be enciphered as itself. Codebreakers slid a guessed phrase (a crib, like 'keine besonderen Ereignisse', nothing to report) along the ciphertext and ruled out every position where a letter landed on itself. The letter pairs at the remaining positions became a 'menu' for Turing's bombe, which ran through all 17,576 rotor positions of one wheel order in about 20 minutes, instead of trying all 158,962,555,217,826,360,000 settings (5 million years at a million a second).

Numbers checked in code, including a working Enigma I simulation that made the ciphertext shown and 100,000 random settings where no letter ever came out as itself. Sources: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptanalysis_of_the_Enigma and en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombe

The math behind real problems, twice a day. Subscribe and the next one finds you.

social_caption: Enigma never turned a letter into itself. That one rule let Bletchley Park rule out guesses and find the day's settings.
facts_checked: A letter could never be encrypted to itself (reflector); used to eliminate a crib in a position; 'keine besonderen Ereignisse' (nothing to report) a stereotyped message; 17,576 scrambler positions; 60 wheel orders (3 of 5 rotors); ten plugboard leads 150,738,274,937,250 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptanalysis_of_the_Enigma)

Turing's bombe design 1939, first bombe March 1940; ~20 minutes to run all 17,576 positions of one rotor order; a self-match is a 'crash'; the menu of letter pairings (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombe)
Total settings 60 x 17,576 x 150,738,274,937,250 = 158,962,555,217,826,360,000; at a million a second about 5 million years (verify.py)
Enigma I simulation (passes the AAAAA -> BDZGO test vector); 100,000 random settings, no letter enciphered as itself (verify.py)
Demo: crib KEINEBESONDERENEREIGNISSE under the 30-letter ciphertext OBISBRPGFQARBSDXIUSVJZQDOHRDRH (seed 0, not cherry-picked): positions 1 and 5 crash, 4 left, the true one is position 4 (verify.py)
One bombe, 60 wheel orders x 20 min = 20 hours (verify.py)

beats.say: Enigma had one flaw. A letter never came out as itself.
Not brute force. 159 billion billion settings. At a million a second, that's 5 million years.
Your job at Bletchley Park, 1940: find today's settings.
First, guess a phrase. Units kept sending nothing to report. In German, that's 25 letters.
Slide it under the message. Wherever a letter lands on itself, that spot is impossible.
Here, two spots crash. Four are left.
But a spot isn't the key. Each letter pair under it is a clue.
Turing's bombe spun through all 17,576 rotor positions, and stopped only where every clue fit. About 20 minutes per rotor order.
5 million years became a day's work. All because a letter could never be itself.
